title: Hanuman Chalisa Meaning: The Opening Verses Explained in Simple English
intro: The Hanuman Chalisa has forty verses written by Tulsidas. Many people recite it daily without knowing the exact meaning. Here are the opening verses in plain words.

p: Shri Guru Charan Saroj Raj, Nij Man Mukur Sudhari. The poet cleans the mirror of his mind with the dust of his guru's lotus feet before he begins.
The next line says he will describe Rama's pure fame, which gives the four goals of life: dharma, artha, kama and moksha.

Buddhiheen tanu janike, sumirau pavan kumar. Knowing that he lacks intelligence, he remembers Hanuman, the son of the wind, and asks for strength, wisdom and knowledge, and for the removal of troubles and flaws.

Jai Hanuman gyan gun sagar: victory to Hanuman, ocean of wisdom and virtue. Ram doot atulit bal dhama: messenger of Rama and home of unmatched strength. Mahabir bikram bajrangi: the great hero of the thunderbolt body who removes bad thinking and keeps company with good thinking.
Tuesdays and Saturdays are popular days. Sit calmly, light a lamp, and read slowly with attention. Understanding the meaning is as valuable as the repetition itself.
Hanuman stands for strength with humility, devotion with courage and service without pride. People turn to the Chalisa for focus and fearlessness.

faq.a: Goswami Tulsidas, in the Awadhi language.

faq.q: How long does it take to recite?
faq.a: About five to eight minutes at a comfortable pace.
